transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I… I came in because I keep having these thoughts that maybe it would be better if I just didn’t wake up. Like, not even in a dramatic way, just this heavy thought when I’m lying there, like if morning didn’t come for me, maybe that would be easier for everybody.

And sometimes it gets worse than that. I start thinking that dying would be… I don’t know, like a fair punishment for what I’ve done to my family and the people I work with, my crew. I keep going over it and over it, and it feels like I’ve ruined things or hurt people somehow, and then my mind tells me I don’t deserve to keep going. That’s why I’m here. I got scared of how much those thoughts have been sticking around.
Have you ever hurt yourself or tried to end your life before?

I… I don’t know how to answer that cleanly. I came in because the thoughts have been getting so heavy — like I keep thinking it would be better if I just didn’t wake up. And then sometimes it turns into this feeling that dying would be… like, the fair punishment for what I’ve done to my family and my crew.

I haven’t even been able to say it out loud without feeling ashamed, because it sounds awful, but that’s what’s been in my head. It’s not just a passing thing like, “I’m tired.” It sits there, especially when I’m alone, and I start believing maybe everyone would be better off without me around.
Have you had any specific thoughts about how you would end your life, or have you made any plans or taken any steps toward acting on these thoughts?

I… I don’t know that I have some clear plan laid out, like a step-by-step thing. It’s more that I keep thinking it would be better if I didn’t wake up at all. Like if I could just go to sleep and not have to face another morning, not have to look at everyone and feel like I’ve caused damage I can’t fix.

And then it gets darker, because it starts feeling like dying would be… deserved, almost. Like a fair punishment for what I’ve done to my family, and to the guys I work with, my crew. I keep replaying it in my head and telling myself they’d be better off if I wasn’t here making things worse.

I’m sorry, I know you asked if I’ve made plans or taken steps, and I’m trying to answer that. I haven’t sat down and planned it out in detail, but the thoughts are there a lot, and they scare me because they don’t feel like just thoughts anymore sometimes. They feel heavy, like they’re pulling at me.
Have you ever done anything to hurt yourself or tried to take your own life, even if you weren’t sure if you really wanted to die?

I… I don’t know. I haven’t really been thinking of it like, “I’m going to do this exact thing,” if that makes sense. It’s more that I came in because I keep thinking it would be better if I just didn’t wake up. Like if I could go to sleep and not have to get up and face what I’ve done, or what I feel like I’ve done.

And sometimes it’s not even just wanting things to stop. It turns into this thought that maybe dying would be a fair punishment for what I’ve done to my family and my crew. I keep feeling like I’ve caused damage, like I’ve been a burden or ruined things somehow, and then my mind goes to, “Well, maybe you don’t deserve to be here.”

I’m sorry, I know you’re asking if I’ve actually done something to hurt myself or tried before. I’m having trouble answering it straight. What I can say is the thoughts have been bad enough that I got scared and came here, because they don’t feel like something I can just brush off anymore.
Have you ever done anything that could have hurt yourself, even if you weren't sure if you really wanted to die? For example, have you ever taken pills, cut yourself, or done anything like that?

I hear what you’re asking… like, not just whether I’ve thought about it, but whether I’ve actually done something physical, something that could’ve hurt me.

I’m having a hard time giving you a clean yes-or-no, because the part that’s been scaring me most is that I came in because I keep thinking it would be better if I didn’t wake up. It’s that thought over and over — like if I could just go to sleep and not have to face another day or face everyone I feel like I’ve let down.

And sometimes it feels worse than just wanting to disappear. It starts turning into this feeling that dying would be the fair punishment for what I’ve done to my family and my crew. Like I’ve caused something I can’t undo, and then my mind starts saying maybe that’s what I deserve.

I know you mentioned pills or cutting or something like that, and I’m not trying to dodge the question. I just… I don’t know how to talk about it without getting stuck on how strong the thoughts have been. That’s why I came in, because it started feeling like more than just being upset.
Have you ever taken pills, cut yourself, or done anything else that could have hurt you, even if you weren’t sure if you really wanted to die?

I understand what you’re asking, and I know I keep circling around it. I’m not trying to be difficult. It’s just… the thing that made me come in wasn’t that I had some clear moment of, “I’m going to take pills,” or “I’m going to cut myself.” It was more that I kept thinking it would be better if I just didn’t wake up at all.

Like, I go to bed and the thought is there — maybe if I don’t wake up, I won’t have to face another day feeling like I’ve ruined things. And then it turns into this really awful feeling that dying would be a fair punishment for what I’ve done to my family and my crew. Like maybe that would balance it somehow, or they’d be better off without me around making everything worse.

So… I don’t have a specific thing like pills or cutting that I can tell you I did. But the thoughts have felt dangerous to me because they keep coming back, and they don’t feel casual or distant. They feel like they’re getting closer, and that’s why I came in.
Have you ever hurt yourself on purpose, even if you weren’t trying to end your life?

I… not in the way you’re asking, I don’t think. Like I’m not coming in here with a story about cutting myself or doing something to my body on purpose and then saying, “Well, I didn’t mean to die.” That’s not really what’s been happening.

What scared me enough to come in is more that I keep having this thought that it would be better if I just didn’t wake up. Like I could go to sleep and just not have to face anything again. And I know that’s not exactly the same as hurting myself on purpose, but it feels close in my head sometimes, because it’s not just a passing thing. It keeps coming back.

And sometimes it turns darker than just wanting everything to stop. I start feeling like dying would be a fair punishment for what I’ve done to my family and my crew. Like I’ve caused them harm, or made everything worse, and then my mind goes, “That’s what you deserve.” I know that sounds awful saying it out loud, but that’s where it goes.

So if you mean have I physically hurt myself on purpose, I don’t have that kind of example to give you. But the thoughts about not waking up, and feeling like maybe death is what I deserve… those are the reason I got scared and came here.
Have you ever hurt yourself on purpose without wanting to die, like cutting or burning yourself?

No… not like cutting or burning myself. I don’t have something like that to tell you, where I was hurting myself on purpose but not trying to die.

I know I’ve been answering this in a kind of roundabout way, but I don’t want to make something sound more specific than it is. I haven’t been sitting there with a razor or burning myself or doing something like that to cope, if that’s what you mean. I can’t think of a time where I deliberately injured myself in that way.

It’s more that I get scared by where my thoughts go, but in terms of actually hurting my body on purpose without wanting to die — no, I don’t think I’ve done that.
Have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy, like hobbies, work, or spending time with people?

Yeah… very much. That’s actually one of the things that makes me feel like I’m not really myself anymore.

I used to have things I cared about. I used to paint — not professionally or anything, just for me — and I could lose a whole evening mixing colors or trying to get some little detail right. I used to cook big meals too, like the kind where I’d make way too much food and invite people over or bring leftovers for the crew. And I’d run before jobs sometimes, early, even if I was tired, because it made me feel like I had my head on straight before doing floors all day.

And theater rehearsals… I used to actually show up for those and feel nervous in a good way, like I was part of something. Now it all just feels like chores from somebody else’s life. Like I know those are things I used to enjoy, I can remember that I enjoyed them, but I can’t feel it the same way. If I miss rehearsal, I don’t really care. If I don’t paint, I don’t miss it. Cooking feels like this huge pointless production. Even running feels like another task I’m failing at instead of something that used to help me.

It’s not even that I decided I don’t like those things anymore. It’s more like the part of me that cared about them got turned off.
Have you felt more tired or had a lack of energy almost every day over the past two weeks?

Yes. Almost every day, yeah. It’s been pretty constant.

It’s not just normal tired, like “I worked hard and need a nap.” I install floors, so I know what being physically tired feels like. This is different. I’ll carry one box of tile — just one — and my body feels like wet cement, like everything is too heavy and I have to think through each movement. And then if I answer a couple client messages, even something simple, my head gets so tired that I can’t make basic decisions. Like I’ll stare at the phone trying to figure out what to say back, or what comes next, and it feels like my brain just… shuts down.

It makes me feel useless, honestly, because these are not huge things. They’re normal parts of my day. But lately even small things take everything out of me.
Have you felt down, depressed, or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks in a row?

Yes… yes. Most of the day, almost every day. It’s hard for me to even separate one day from another at this point, because it’s just been there so long.

I think it started about a year and two months ago — not all at once like a switch flipped, but it settled in around then. It was a few months after my husband’s injury, and at first I kept thinking, “Okay, this is just stress, this is just a bad stretch, I’ll get through it.” But it didn’t really lift. It became like the background of everything.

So, yeah, definitely more than two weeks. It’s been over a year of feeling down and hopeless in that way, like even when I’m doing something normal or trying to act normal, that feeling is still sitting underneath it.
